                     </ns0:gap> 4.19. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 14.</ns0:note> which was a prophet mighty in deed and word be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore God, and all the people:<ns0:note place="bottom">The things which had lately happened in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> were so many, and so unusual, that the Disciples wonder that any one coming from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> should ask what things? they therefore ask him, if he were a meer stranger in <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> coming from some other Country, or from some remoter parts of <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Galilee?</ns0:hi> or, if he were the only Man, who had been unconcerned in what was the common Discourse, both of the Town and Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try? Still our Saviour draws out the Discourse from them, by asking them what things? They tell them concerning <ns0:hi>Iesus of Nazareth,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>great Prophet, mighty both in Words and Deeds.</ns0:hi> In which Phrase <ns0:hi>Stephen</ns0:hi> Celebrated <ns0:hi>Moses, Acts</ns0:hi> 7.22. That is, one who did not only in an Extraordinary manner reveal the Will of God unto Men, but also did many great and mighty Works, and lived a most Holy and most Exemplary Life, and Conversation, so as that he was not only highly favoured of God. but in great repute, and Estimation also amongst the Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 And how the chief priests and our rulers de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />livered him to be condemned to death, and have cru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cified him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 But we trusted that it had been he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ts 1.6.</ns0:note> which should have redeemed Israel: And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is from hence evident, that as yet they neither had a true Notion of Christ as <ns0:hi>God-man</ns0:hi> in one Person, nor yet of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> but still remain'd in an opinion of a Temporal Deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verance, to be effected for the Jews by the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> when he should come. The Words also shewed a great weakness in the Disciples Faith as to Christ they speak as if they were quite out of Breath, and their Faith began to fail. We were say they once of the mind, and maintained some Hope that <ns0:hi>this Iesus of Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />zareth,</ns0:hi> had been he whom God had designed for the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> and now <ns0:hi>it is the third Day since these things were done.</ns0:hi> This mention of the <ns0:hi>third Day,</ns0:hi> is a good Argument to prove that these were some old Disciples of Christ, who had taken notice of his <ns0:hi>Promise</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Prophecy,</ns0:hi> that he should <ns0:hi>Rise again the third Day, Chap.</ns0:hi> 18.33. They ought to have had patience till Night, and to have considered, that tho the third Day were began, yet it was not yet past.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Yea, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 28.8. Mark 16.10. John 20.18.</ns0:note> certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chre.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 And when they found not his body, they came, saying that they had also seen a vision of angels which said that he was alive.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 And certain of them which were with us, went to the sepulchre, and found <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> even so as the women had said; but him they saw not.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is plain from the Relation of these two Disciples, that they had whatsoever might conduce to a <ns0:hi>Moral Suasion.</ns0:hi> They had the <ns0:hi>Revelation of the Word,</ns0:hi> from the Mouth of Christ himself. They had Evidences from the Women, from the <ns0:hi>Apparition</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> from some among themselves, that his Body was not there. The Angels said he was Risen. Why do they hesitate then? Why do they not believe? is the fault in the <ns0:hi>Perverseness of their Wills</ns0:hi>? had they no mind to believe, that the thing they had hoped, longed, waited for, was true? Certainly there was no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thing they more desired. Let the Patrons of the Power of Man's Will to believe, or perform any Actions Spiritually good, tell us (if they can) what could hinder these Disciples actual be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving the Resurrection of Christ, but the <ns0:hi>Impotency</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Wills,</ns0:hi> God not yet pleasing to Influence, and assist their Wills actually to believe, what they had the greatest Propensions, and Inclinations imaginable to have believed.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 26. Acts 17.3. 1 Pet. 1.11.</ns0:note> Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And beginning at <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 3.15. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 22.18. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 26 4 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 49.10. Deut. 18.15.</ns0:note> and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 132.11. Isa. 7.14 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.6 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 40.10. Jer. 23.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 33.14. Ezek. 34.23. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 37.25. Dan. 9.24. Mich. 7.20. <ns0:hi>See on</ns0:hi> John 1.45.</ns0:note> all the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures, the things concerning himself.<ns0:note place="bottom">By our Saviour's form of reprehending his Disciples, We may both learn. 1. That it is not every saying, <ns0:hi>Thou Fool,</ns0:hi> but a saying of it from a Root of hatred, Malice and Anger, which our Saviour makes to be a Breach of the sixth Commandment, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 5. Our Saviour's Reprehension of them was out of a Principle of Love, and a Root of good Will to them. 2. <ns0:hi>That the best of us are very slow of Heart to believe what cometh to us upon the meer credit of a Divine Revelation.</ns0:hi> It is also observable from what we have, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 27. That <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> and the Prophets are not to be rejected by Christians, they also have much concern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Christ; out of them Christ instructeth these two Disciples in the things concerning himself.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> Gen. 32.26.</ns0:note> made as though he would have gone further.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 19 3. Acts 16.15.</ns0:note> they constrained him, saying, Abide with us, for it is towards evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.<ns0:note place="bottom">I do not understand how some conclude from hence the lawfulness of dissembling, or telling a lye in some Cases, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause the Evangelist saith, our Saviour made as tho he would have gone further, and did not; for without doubt our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our had gone further, if the Disciples had not been urgent with him to have staid. Nor did he stay long there, as we shall hear by and by.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And it came to pass as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and brake, and gave to them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>he ceased to be seen of them.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> he vanished out of of their sight.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some would have this Bread to be <ns0:hi>Sacramental Bread,</ns0:hi> as if our Lord at this time Celebrated his Supper, and some of the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> are mightily Zealous for that Interpretation, thinking that they have in it a mighty Argument, to justify their Lame Administration of it <ns0:hi>in one kind</ns0:hi> (for here is no mention of the Cup at all) but they do not consider, that this Text will prove (if it be taken with relation to the <ns0:hi>Supper</ns0:hi>) more than they would have it, as, 1. That priests may Consecrate, with<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />out Wine, which themselves will not grant, tho they say that both Elements being Consecrated, the People sufficiently <ns0:hi>par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />take</ns0:hi> if they share but in one. 2. It will also prove that a Priest may Consecrate, without useing those substantial Words <ns0:hi>This is my Body.</ns0:hi> But it is a most improbable thing, that our Saviour coming just out of his Journey, should fall upon his Administra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of this Ordinance. The Text is certainly to be meant of Bodily Bread, which our Saviour never took without a previous Blessing of it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 14.19. How their Eyes were opened, the Evangelist tells us. Some think they knew him by his form of Blessing. It is a wonder then they did not know him before by his Style, in three or four Hours Discourse by the way. O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers think they knew him by taking upon him the Office of the Master of the Feast. <ns0:hi>To bless the Table,</ns0:hi> and to C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rve to the Guests. But all this is vain, He withdrew the Ve<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l from their Eyes, which alone hindred their discerning him before, for the Object was visible, only the Medium of their sight was indis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />posed, <ns0:hi>And he vanished out of their sight.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour had now obtained his end, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to satisfy them that he was indeed risen, now he disappeareth, for that he had a power to make his Body inperceptable to the Disciples Senses is out of doubt.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:326" />32 And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures.<ns0:note place="bottom">There was a mighty difference no doubt, betwixt Christ's Preaching, and his Ministers; he Preached as one who had Autho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity, not as the Scribes, not as ordinary Ministers, but with more <ns0:hi>Majesty</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi>; but as to the saving Efficacy of his Words, that depended upon his <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> where he pleased to put forth such Efficacious Grace, there his Words became effectual, where he did not, they were not so: Christ Preached in the hearing of hundreds, who yet continued Unbelievers, and Perished in their Unbelief. There is a great deal of difference also between one Minister's Preaching and anothers; some kind of Preaching of its self, makes Mens Hearts to Freeze, others make them to Burn, but where Preaching makes our Hearts to Burn within us, Christ throws in the Coal, which the best Preacher doth but blow up: only the Spirit of God is pleased to Work (as <ns0:hi>Eras<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mus</ns0:hi> saith) <ns0:hi>secundum quod nactus est Organon,</ns0:hi> according to the Instrument it worketh by, and to Concur with Rational and Spiritual means, in order to Rational and Spiritual ends. But wherever any Soul is Baptized <ns0:hi>with Fire</ns0:hi> at hearing a Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon, it is also <ns0:hi>Baptized with the Holy Ghost.</ns0:hi> Christ will not always Cure Blind Eyes with <ns0:hi>Clay</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Spittle</ns0:hi> (tho he did it once.) These were Disciples before the Fire was kindled in their Hearts, Christ's Preaching did but blow it up. We ought so to speak in our Preaching, so to open, and apply the Scriptures as our Discourses, may have a rational tendency, to make the Hearts of our hearers <ns0:hi>to Burn</ns0:hi> within them, not so as to make them Dead, and Sleepy, and Cold, or luke-warm: and then to know that it must be Christ's Work to Inflame them, when we have said all that we can say.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />peared to Simon.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 And they told what things <ns0:hi>were done</ns0:hi> in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.<ns0:note place="bottom">The 34. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> compared with, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.5. makes some great Authors think, that <ns0:hi>Simon</ns0:hi> was one of the <ns0:hi>two,</ns0:hi> and that <ns0:hi>Cle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />opas</ns0:hi> (who was the other) spake this. They make no stay at <ns0:hi>Emmaus,</ns0:hi> but come presently to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> and acquaint the Disciples, That for certain Christ was Risen, and that he had appeared to them in the way, and was known of them at their breaking of Bread.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And as they thus spake, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> unto you.<ns0:note place="bottom">Of this appearance of Christ, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> speaks, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 16.14. and <ns0:hi>Iohn, Ch.</ns0:hi> 20.19, 20. The Salutation, which he useth to them was common amongst the Jews, and answereth our <ns0:hi>God save you,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>God be with you.</ns0:hi> It was an apprecation of all Blessing, and Happiness, which they comprehended under the name of <ns0:hi>Peace.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.<ns0:note place="bottom">Spirits sometimes (by Gods permission, or direction) assu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med humane shapes. They seeing an humane shape, and not able on the sudden to conceive, how an humane Body should come into the midst amongst them, without any more noise, or notice taken of it, were affrighted, as we usually are, at the sight of apprehended Apparations. From hence we may con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clude, That either the World, and the best Men in it, have been in all Ages deceived, and a few <ns0:hi>Atheists</ns0:hi> have been wiser than them all, or there are such Beings as <ns0:hi>Spirits.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And he said unto them, Why are ye troubled, and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I my self: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 20.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.27.</ns0:note> handle me, and see, for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 And when he had thus spoken, he shewed them <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> hands and <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> feet.<ns0:note place="bottom">If either the <ns0:hi>Papists,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> could shew us Christ's <ns0:hi>Hands</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Feet,</ns0:hi> while they impose upon us to believe, that Christ's Body is <ns0:hi>really</ns0:hi> present at, or in the Lord's Supper, they would not so <ns0:hi>fright us,</ns0:hi> nor make so many thoughts arise in us as they do, about their apprehensions of the <ns0:hi>Nature of a Body.</ns0:hi> But while the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> allow us to <ns0:hi>Handle,</ns0:hi> and to t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>st the <ns0:hi>Bread,</ns0:hi> and we find no such things, and the <ns0:hi>Lutherans</ns0:hi> suffer our Eyes to be open, and we can see no such thing. We cannot but conclude, that the <ns0:hi>Body of Christ</ns0:hi> which they talk of, must certainly be a Spirit, which (according to our Saviour's notion) is a substance which <ns0:hi>hath neither Flesh nor Bones,</ns0:hi> as we see the Body, they would have us to believe hath not; that is to say, that <ns0:hi>the Body</ns0:hi> they talk of, <ns0:hi>is no Body.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour here proveth that it was his <ns0:hi>true Body</ns0:hi> which appeared to them, because, 1. It had <ns0:hi>Inte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gral parts,</ns0:hi> Hands and Feet. 2. Because it might be seen. 3. It might be handled. 4. It had Flesh and Bones, which a Spirit hath not. Then he shews them his Hands and Feet. So then our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />our did not think, that the Judgment of our Senses was to be rejected, concerning the Nature of Bodies, and his Body in par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular, and that in its <ns0:hi>State of Exaltation,</ns0:hi> when it was raised from the Dead. Do any of them say that <ns0:hi>Christ's Body</ns0:hi> here came through the Door, or it could not have been here? How shall that be proved? We can easily tell them how his Body might be in the midst of them, tho it were not discerned while he was there, even as the Eyes of the two Disciples were held, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 16. that they could not discern Christ, so the Eyes of the Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples might be <ns0:hi>held now,</ns0:hi> till he was in the midst amongst them.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondred, he said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 21.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> Have ye here any meat?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honey-comb.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 And he took <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> and did eat before them.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Believed not for Ioy,</ns0:hi> yet if they had not now believed, they doubtless would not have rejoyced, but their Faith was the cause of their Joy; yet the Excess of their Joy was the hinderance of their Faith, so dangerous are the excessive motions of our Af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fections. Christ here gives them another Evidence of the truth of his Body, he did Eat with them, (tho very ordinary Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />try Diet a piece of broiled Fish, and a piece of an Honey-comb) such a Meal as we read of that he had at the Lake of <ns0:hi>Tiberias, Iohn</ns0:hi> 21.9. He did not Eat to <ns0:hi>uphold,</ns0:hi> but only to <ns0:hi>testify</ns0:hi> his Life. Thus when he had raised the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Iairus, Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.55. he bid them <ns0:hi>give her something to Eat</ns0:hi>; and for this end <ns0:hi>Lazarus</ns0:hi> sate at <ns0:hi>Meat</ns0:hi> with the rest, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.2. and <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> proves the Resurrection of Christ from their Eating and Drink<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing with him, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.41. Let not profane Wits seek Knots in Bulrushes, inquiring what became of this Meat? <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Let them first tell us what became of the Meat the <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> did Eat with <ns0:hi>Abraham, Gen.</ns0:hi> 18.8. and learn to believe, that it was easie with the Power of God to Annihilate again that Meat, which was not necessary for the fustentation the body ofChrist, now freed from all the cravings of Natural Appetite, tho he did Eat it to sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tisfy them, that he was truly risen from the Dead.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 And he said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Ver. 6.</ns0:note> These <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled which were written
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:326" />
in the law of Moses, and <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> the prophets, and <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> the psalms concerning me.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Jews ordinarily divided the Old Testament into the <ns0:hi>Law,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Holy Writings,</ns0:hi> which they called the <ns0:hi>Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />giographa.</ns0:hi> The Book of <ns0:hi>Psalms</ns0:hi> was one of the last sort, and one of the most noted amongst them: so as by these three Terms our Saviour understands all the Scriptures of the Old Testament. He tells them, that he had before his Death, while he Conversed with them, told them that <ns0:hi>all things</ns0:hi> (which were very many) which were found in any of these Books con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning him must be fulfilled, he had told them so, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 18.31. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 16.21. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 17.22. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 20.18. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 9.31. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.34.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.<ns0:note place="bottom">He did not open their Understanding, without the Scriptures, he sends them thither, and he knew the Scriptures would not suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ficiently give them a Knowledge of him, and the things of God, without th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Influence, and Illumination of his Spirit, they are truly taught of God, who are taught by his Spirit to under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand the Scriptures. Christ gives a great Honour to the <ns0:hi>Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures.</ns0:hi> The Devil Cheats those Souls whom he persuades to cast away the Scriptures in Expectation of a teaching by the Spirit. The Spirit teacheth by, not without, not contrary to the Holy Scriptures.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 And said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psals 22. Isa 53. Acts 17.3.</ns0:note> Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day.<ns0:note place="bottom">All the Divine Predictions are certain, and infallible. The Jews did Maliciously and freely prosecute our Saviour to Death, and God did certainly foresee how their Wills would be deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mined, and the Event was accomplished accordingly.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 And that repentance, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 John 2.12.</ns0:note> remission of sins should be preached in his name, amongst all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">48 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">John 15.27.</ns0:note> ye are witnesses of these things.<ns0:note place="bottom">The few Words in <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 47. are comprehensive of the great duty of the Apostles, 1. <ns0:hi>To preach Repentance and Remission of Sins.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>In Christs Name.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>To all Nations.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>Beginning at Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> They were to Preach <ns0:hi>Repentance,</ns0:hi> that is, a turning from Sinful Courses, into a Course of Life Consonant to the Will of God, and <ns0:hi>Remission of Sins,</ns0:hi> that is, upon <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pentance,</ns0:hi> this they were to <ns0:hi>Preach in his Name,</ns0:hi> which may refer either to their <ns0:hi>Preaching</ns0:hi>; then our Saviour lets them know that they were to be his Ministers, and to Preach by his <ns0:hi>Autho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.20. To be <ns0:hi>Ambassadours for Christ, Stewards of his Mysteries.</ns0:hi> Or else it may refer to <ns0:hi>Repentance</ns0:hi> and Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mission of Sins, which are to be Preached <ns0:hi>in his Name,</ns0:hi> for the sake of Merits and Satisfaction. They were to Preach this <ns0:hi>to all Nations.</ns0:hi> This was prophesied of plentifully, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 2.8. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 49.6. <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 7.14. <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 2.23. <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 2.32. This was a piece of Divine Revelation, which Christ had, till this time, concealed in a great Measure, when he sent out the Twelve, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.5. He commanded them not to go to the Gentiles. <ns0:hi>Beginning at Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> that is, amongst the Jews. He was prophesied of under the Notion of a <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> to be set <ns0:hi>upon the Lords Holy Hill of Sion.</ns0:hi> So <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110.2. <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 2.3. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 28.16. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 60. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1. in pursuance of this, we shall find <ns0:hi>the Apostles</ns0:hi> Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing only in <ns0:hi>Iudea,</ns0:hi> till they had judged themselves <ns0:hi>unworthy of Eternal Life, then they turned to the Gentiles, Acts</ns0:hi> 13.38.46.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

                     </ns0:gap> 16.17: Acts 1.4. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>er. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> I send the promise of my fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem, until ye be indued with power from on high.<ns0:note place="bottom">It is questioned by none, but by the <ns0:hi>promise of the Father,</ns0:hi> our Lord meaneth the <ns0:hi>promise of the Spirit,</ns0:hi> as it came down in the Days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost.</ns0:hi> This Effusion of the Spirit was pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised under the Old Testament, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 44.3. <ns0:hi>Ierem.</ns0:hi> 31.33. <ns0:hi>Ezech.</ns0:hi> 36.27. Most eminently, <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 2.28. (The Apostle himself interpreting the Prophets. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.16, 17, 18:) See also <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.8. Where the fulfilling of this <ns0:hi>promise of the Father,</ns0:hi> as it is call'd, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. is put before—<ns0:hi>and ye shall be Witnesses unto me, both in Ierusalem, and in Iudea, and in Samaria,</ns0:hi> and is also expounded by, <ns0:hi>And ye shall receive Power, after the Holy Ghost is come upon you.</ns0:hi> Our Lord also had said, <ns0:hi>I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever.</ns0:hi> In this Text he saith, <ns0:hi>that he will send him</ns0:hi>; so also <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 15.26. and <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 16.7. there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by confirming his Disciples in this, That he was equal with the Father, and that the Holy Ghost was sent by the Father and him, yet sent <ns0:hi>by the Father upon the Prayer of the Son, and in his Name, Iohn</ns0:hi> 14.16, 26. This Holy Spirit is also called <ns0:hi>Po<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wer from on high, the power of the highest, Luke</ns0:hi> 1.35. But here the <ns0:hi>Gifts of the Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> may be understood as also in <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.8. where this <ns0:hi>Power</ns0:hi> is said <ns0:hi>should be received af<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>er that the Holy Ghost should come upon them,</ns0:hi> until this time should come, which was in the Days of <ns0:hi>Pentecost, Acts</ns0:hi> 2.1. The Disciples were bound to <ns0:hi>stay at Ierusalem</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> which accord<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ingly they did. And we may from hence conclude, that these Words of our <ns0:hi>Saviour</ns0:hi> were spoken to his Disciples, after his appearance to them in <ns0:hi>Gallilee,</ns0:hi> (of which <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith nothing) which was the place where (as most think) he was seen of <ns0:hi>above five hundred Brethren at once,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.6.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 And he led them out as far as to Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thany: and he lift up his hands, and blessed them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 16.19:</ns0:note> And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">This must be understood to have happened for<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty days after our Saviour's Resurrection, for so <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> himself tells us, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.3. then he led them out as far as <ns0:hi>Bethany,</ns0:hi> not the Village <ns0:hi>Bethany,</ns0:hi> but that part of the Mount of <ns0:hi>Olives,</ns0:hi> which belonged to <ns0:hi>Bethany.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour had been often there praying, from thence, he now ascendeth into Heaven, <ns0:hi>and l<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>f<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted up his Hands and blessed them.</ns0:hi> Some think that by <ns0:hi>Blessing,</ns0:hi> here is meant <ns0:hi>Praying</ns0:hi>; and the <ns0:hi>lifting up of his Hands,</ns0:hi> was accommodated to that religious Action. Others think that <ns0:hi>Blessing</ns0:hi> here signifieth a more <ns0:hi>Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thoritative Act</ns0:hi>; and that his lifting up of his Hands, was a stretching out of his Hands, as a sign of that effectual Blessing of them. <ns0:hi>While he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up to Heaven,</ns0:hi> that is, he moved upward, as if he had been carri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, for it is certain that our Saviour <ns0:hi>ascended</ns0:hi> by his own Power. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.9. <ns0:hi>He was taken up and a Cloud received him out of <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>heir sight,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Elijah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 2.11. <ns0:hi>Went up to Heaven in a Whirle-wind.</ns0:hi> So Christ went up in a Cloud, but with this difference Christ ascended by his own power, <ns0:hi>Elijah</ns0:hi> could not without the help of an Angel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.<ns0:note place="bottom">We never before read of any Act of <ns0:hi>Adoration,</ns0:hi> which the Disciples performed to Christ. Their Faith was now come to the highest pitch. They did no longer look upon him only as one <ns0:hi>sent of God, a great Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet,</ns0:hi> nor only as the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> the promised <ns0:hi>Mes<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sias.</ns0:hi> In the mean time not rightly taking the notion of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> but looking upon him as one who should be a <ns0:hi>Temporal Saviour,</ns0:hi> and deliverer of his People, they now believe him to be the <ns0:hi>Eternal Son of God,</ns0:hi> being so manifested by his <ns0:hi>Resurrection from the Dead,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ascension into Heaven</ns0:hi> before their Eyes. According to his Commandment they return to <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem,</ns0:hi> full of Joy. <ns0:hi>And were continually in the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple praising and blessing God,</ns0:hi> Amen, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.12, 13. it is said, that they being returned, they went into an <ns0:hi>upper Room,</ns0:hi> and continued in <ns0:hi>Prayer</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Suppli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation.</ns0:hi> Some think that this <ns0:hi>upper Room,</ns0:hi> was ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pendant to the Temple. But <ns0:hi>continually</ns0:hi> here may reasonably be interpreted often, or ordinarily, or at <ns0:hi>Temple Hours</ns0:hi> of prayer as the <ns0:hi>Morning,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Even<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Sacrifice,</ns0:hi> are called the <ns0:hi>Continual Burnt-Offering, Exod.</ns0:hi> 29.42. <ns0:hi>Num.</ns0:hi> 28.3. Their work was to <ns0:hi>praise</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Bless God.</ns0:hi> It is not said for what, but ea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sily understood: as for other mercies, so more espe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cially for his sending the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> for our <ns0:hi>Redemption,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Confirmation,</ns0:hi> and perfecting their <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in him.</ns0:note>
